items.issues: Must link the flour-shortage sentence to the rereading; D is the result-as-motive misread as intended. B is a reasonable second pull but the text gives the chemist no role in blame.
Coat/boots sentence plus 'without telling her' make D direct; B (gratitude/stay longer) is the result-as-motive distractor but 'without telling her' kills it quickly. C invents facts.
Weight judgment (laughing, side-by-side work vs one touched marker) is clear; B/C are weight-wrong, D is a scope-wrong distractor. Solid.

'He laughed, but she did not' plus the punched dough tilt toward indignation as dominant; A is a close weight-inverted distractor that some students will pick, which is the intended design, not a flaw.
'And still I lifted my basket higher' settles defiance as dominant over fear; A is the weight-inverted distractor, B the pre-turn tone. Works.
Frame ('Years ago', 'carried the phrase for years, twelve then thirteen') makes reflection dominant; A inverts weight, C narrows scope, B contradicts 'Even so'.

'Yet ... as though each careful join were a promise' makes devotion primary; B inverts, C narrows to the cinema, D is off. D is slightly weak but still a tone word a careless reader could grab from 'friends since childhood'.
B (nurse depends on patient for chores) is not a serious distractor; A and C are fine. Answer is nearly spelled out by 'the only one here who does not finish my sentences'.

All three distractors share one misconception (narrator wants credit / Kwame withholds it) that the first sentence already contradicts; C and D overlap. Needs at least one distractor from a different angle.

The bush can be read as the belated apology (B) or as Ximena herself, wounded by late action and 'bitter' (C) — 'Some take longer' and Ximena tending the bush support both. Stem or options need tightening so only one reading survives.
'I did not know how long I would stay' + checking the graft 'like a pulse' + the shoot make C direct. D is a stretch but harmless.
'Neither of them ever spoke of it' hands over the answer; C is a partial read (Karim alone), B/D are scope misreads. Clean but easy.
'Still burning above the water long after the lodge had vanished' points straight to B; C is the nearest misread (fear vs care). Fine.
The simile is glossed in the same sentence ('heavy and impossible to haul up alone'), so C is almost a paraphrase. D plays on the literal 'anchor = steadying' misread, which is a good distractor.
Second stanza ('bob near the surface... refusing to drown') restates the answer. C overreaches, B/D invert. Clean.
'A menu that served both' resolves it. C (friendship) is a reasonable off-target reading; A/D invert. Fine.
'Walking beside it with great care' and the hawk deflections make C direct; B is the literal-reading trap, A/D are not supported. Fine.
'Then she stopped skimming' marks the pivot explicitly; A/B/C all misname the starting tone. Fine for medium-low.
'Trying not to smile' then 'quite softly... father had been a foreman' is clear; B/C/D misname both ends. Clean.
Needs the tin-box sentence plus 'as if no account had ever been open'; B is the anecdote-summary partial as designed, C/D are scope/moral overreaches. Fine.
